# pciutils

**lspci — for the SDRs and capture cards that are not on USB**

- **Version recorded:** 3.13.0
- **Categories:** `device-support`, `workstation`
- **Upstream:** <https://mj.ucw.cz/sw/pciutils/>

## What it does

Lists PCI and PCIe devices with their identifiers, drivers in use, and resource assignments.

## Why you would want it

Not every SDR is a USB dongle. LimeSDR XTRX and Red Pitaya-class hardware sit on PCIe, and 'which driver claimed this device' is a question only lspci -k answers. It is also how you check whether a kernel module bound at all.

## Before it will work

Nothing.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`workstation`](../profiles/workstation.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install pciutils --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `pciutils`

## Known problems

Device names come from a pci.ids database that ages; a very new card may show as an unrecognised vendor and product number, which is cosmetic rather than a fault.
